A team of 5 open-weight 27B models just outscored Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard.

🤖 Memdoor introduced an agent workflow combining 5 Qwen3.8-27B models that surpassed Fable 5 performance on LiveCodeBench Hard coding benchmarks.

This shows how specialized multi-model orchestrations are continuing to push coding performance without relying strictly on a single closed proprietary backend.

⚙️ Factory released Droid 1.0, a model-independent coding agent harness built around script mode and programmatic tool calling.

In Terminal-Bench 4 testing, Droid scored 65.2% when paired with Claude Opus 5.5, averaging $4.73 per passed task.

💻 Nace AI open-sourced Drex Max v1, a 27B multimodal decision model that scores 67.52 and runs locally on Apple Silicon hardware.

Having a model of this scale geared for decision tasks directly on consumer hardware opens up fresh options for local deployment.

🧠 Developer discussions on r/LocalLLaMA highlight a shift away from llama.cpp toward newer bespoke engines like Strata for local model benchmarks.

Engine performance for local execution is evolving quickly as developers hit token budget limits on cloud API providers.

Are you moving toward orchestrated teams of smaller models, or still relying primarily on single large foundation models for your dev workflows?
